title: 1 Simple Thing #1:
title_short: 1 Simple Thing #1 · Check Your Voter Registration
headline: A real person checks her voter registration in 32 seconds, so the viewer knows they can do it too.
story: Rebecca from WNY Women's Foundation recorded her own screen while she checked her registration on the New York State site. Her voice file explains each step: county, last name, first name, date of birth, zip code, search. The result says Voter Status: Active. This is week 1 of the client's new “1 Simple Thing” series.

The client asked for two things in writing: keep it in real time, so people see how easy it is, and blur her personal voting information. It must feel calm, simple and doable. Strictly non-partisan: no party, no candidate, no issue.
do: Open on frame 1 with the moving form and <q>THIS TAKES 32 SECONDS.</q> No logo, no title image, no fade.
Play the recording in real time. When the voice is longer, hold a still frame.
Blur every value she types and every autofill pop-up. Keep the field names sharp.
Keep Voter Status : Active sharp. Arrive on it when she says “active”.
Write the site as voterlookup.elections.ny.gov every time.
dont: Never show her name, birth date, zip, address, party or district numbers. Not for one frame.
Do not speed up the recording. Do not cut inside REC 0:00–0:20.
No new voice-over. Only Main St.m4a.
No party, candidate or issue words. No DEI words.
